bihar_raw_news.content: Home > Business > Bihar rolls out red carpet for renewable energy investors Business Bihar rolls out red carpet for renewable energy investors BY Mpost Bureau 5 Nov 2026 1:02 AM IST X Mpost Bureau 5 Nov 2026 1:02 AM IST New Delhi: Bihar on Wednesday pitched investment opportunities worth Rs 2.57 lakh crore in its power sector, inviting domestic and international investors to explore projects in renewable energy, storage, transmission and distribution. Addressing the Bihar State Plenary Session at the India Renewable Energy Summit and Expo 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, state Energy Minister Shailesh Kumar alias Bulo Mandal assured investors of all possible support from the government and said Bihar offered significant potential for high growth and returns. He said the state’s electricity demand had increased from around 700 MW in 2005 to nearly 10,000 MW, with every household now having electricity connectivity. Energy Secretary and Bihar State Power Holding Company Ltd (BSPHCL) CMD Ajay Yadav said demand was projected to reach 25,000 MW over the next decade. He highlighted the 301 MW Kajra Solar Power Project, supported by a 523 MWh battery energy storage system, and said projects worth Rs 78,400 crore were at various stages of implementation. Under the Bihar Renewable Energy Policy 2025, the state has set a target of developing 24 GW renewable energy capacity and 6 GWh energy storage capacity by 2030. A comprehensive investment roadmap of Rs 2,57,316 crore has also been prepared. Three MoUs were signed during the summit involving BSPGCL, MANIT Bhopal, the Power Sector Skill Council, BSPHCL, Bihar Power Training Management Society and TERI to promote renewable energy. bihar_raw_news.title: Patna-Purnia Expressway May Get Launch Nod During PM's Vaishali Visit - Urban Acres
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Patna-Purnia Expressway May Get Launch Nod During PM’s Vaishali Visit Breaking News Patna-Purnia Expressway May Get Launch Nod During PM’s Vaishali Visit By Ayesha Siddiqui November 5, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Prime Minister Narendra Modi is expected to visit Vaishali on November 20 for a public programme where he may launch or lay the foundation for several Bihar development projects, including the proposed Patna-Purnia Expressway, according to state BJP leaders quoted by the Times of India. The proposed National Expressway-9, described as Bihar’s first national expressway project, is planned as a six-lane greenfield corridor. It will begin at Mirnagar in Vaishali district and pass through Samastipur, Darbhanga, Saharsa and Madhepura before ending at Chand Bhatti in Purnia district. The details of the proposed visit and project programme were shared by BJP functionaries ahead of the planned event. The report said the Prime Minister was scheduled to participate in a public programme at the Jafarpatti Industrial Area in Vaishali, although the project launches were described as expected or likely rather than formally confirmed through a government notification. Bihar BJP president Sanjay Saraogi inspected the proposed venue and reviewed arrangements with officials. He also discussed logistical preparations and directed those involved in organising the programme to ensure its smooth conduct. BJP MLAs Awadhesh Singh and Sanjay Singh, along with Janata Dal (United) MLA Siddharth Patel, were present during the inspection. The Patna-Purnia corridor would connect central and northern parts of Bihar through a route crossing several districts. The proposed alignment includes Samastipur, Darbhanga, Saharsa and Madhepura, placing the expressway within a wider regional transport network linking Vaishali with Purnia in eastern Bihar. The Prime Minister is also expected to inaugurate or lay foundation stones for projects in Bhagalpur and Banka districts during the programme. These may include a proposed Central University near Vikramshila and the proposed Ajgaibinath Greenfield Airport near Sultanganj in Bhagalpur district. Saraogi said the visit would provide fresh momentum to development initiatives in Bihar and help accelerate investment and infrastructure growth in the state. The source report did not provide the expressway’s construction cost, completion schedule, land-acquisition status, detailed interchange plan or traffic projections. Further details about the final project list, the formal launch arrangements and the implementation timelines are expected to be clarified ahead of the proposed November 20 programme. national_raw_news.title: Democrats secure control of both houses of Congress in US Midterm elections, winning 54 seats in ...
national_raw_news.content: In the US midterm elections, the Democratic Party secured 54 seats out of 100 seats in the Senate, gaining control of the upper chamber of Congress following a series of electoral victories. In the House of Representatives, the Democratic Party have also crossed the threshold of 218 seats required to win the majority as it won 224 seats, while the Republican Party secured 135 of the 435 seats. The counting of ballots is underway. The Democratic Party registered significant gains in several traditionally Republican states. In South Carolina, Democratic candidate and doctor Annie Andrews defeated Republican Darline Graham to win a Senate seat. The state had not elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1998. In neighbouring North Carolina, former Governor and Democratic candidate Roy Cooper defeated Republican Michael Whatley, securing another Senate seat for his party. In Texas, Democratic candidate and seminarian James Talarico defeated State Attorney General Ken Paxton. This marks a significant development in a state where Democrats have not won a statewide election since 1994. Meanwhile, in Ohio, Democrat Sherrod Brown defeated incumbent Republican Senator Jon Husted. In Kansas, Democratic pastor Adam Hamilton also defeated sitting Republican Senator Roger Marshall. Reacting to the election results, US President Donald Trump said that he will accept the results. Polling was held for all 435 seats in the US House of Representatives, 35 of the 100 seats in the Senate, and 36 governorships. The Democratic victory is expected to have a significant impact on the remaining term of President Donald Trump, particularly on the functioning of the US Congress and the legislative agenda of his administration.

national_raw_news.content: Cabinet today approved the ‘Viksit Bharat Initiative for Statistical Transformation, Analytics & Research, VISTAR Scheme for 2026-27 to 2030-31 with an outlay of over 4,371 crore rupees. The VISTAR Scheme is designed to establish a dynamic, real-time and future-ready official statistical architecture for enhanced timeliness, data granularity, interoperability with harmonised and AI-ready datasets. It will provide the strategic flexibility to dynamically allocate resources based on immediate policy needs, fostering a holistic approach to large-scale survey execution, methodological research, digital transformation, and national data governance. VISTAR Scheme will encompass all statistical and data management activities of Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation. It will play a crucial role for upgrading the official statistical system of the country. The Cabinet has also approved the ‘Capex Support Scheme to Promote Critical Mineral Processing’ with a financial outlay of two thousand 814 crore rupees over a period of five years. Processing of critical minerals remains geographically concentrated in a few global locations. This exposes supply chains to geopolitical disruptions, price volatility, and potential supply restrictions, posing severe threats to supply chain resilience and economic security. This has implications for national security, economic sovereignty, and the timely achievement of decarbonisation targets. The “Capex Support Scheme to Promote Critical Mineral Processing” has been formulated to provide targeted capital expenditure support for the establishment and operationalisation of domestic processing facilities.

national_raw_news.title: Agniveers get two-year extension as Cabinet approves extension of service period
national_raw_news.content: The Union Cabinet has approved two year extension for Agniveers who were earlier set to exit after four years of service. Briefing media after the Union Cabinet meeting in New Delhi today, CDS General NS Raja Subramani said, 75 per cent of Agniveers who had to exit will now be given an additional two-year engagement period, after which the willing Agniveers can enrol in the Armed Forces. He stated that the first batch of Agniveers is now nearing the completion of their four-year tenure. He said, based on the performance evaluations conducted over these four years, Army has received positive feedback about their performance. He said that 25 per cent of the Agniveers are to be enrolled into the regular forces based on merit. General Raja Subramani said that under the scheme, the remaining 75 percent of Agniveers will now be offered an additional engagement period of two years. He said, upon the completion of this two-year period, all those Agniveers who are willing to continue will be enrolled into the Armed Forces. He said, the extension will come with higher remuneration. General Raja Subramani said that the Agnipath scheme was introduced on 14th June, 2022. He said, earlier it was decided that Agniveers would undergo continuous performance evaluations and that the scheme will be reviewed periodically. General Raja Subramani said that the recruitment footprint under the Agnipath Scheme has expanded and Agniveers are being enrolled in almost all districts across the country. He said the recruitment process has become more transparent and streamlined.

national_raw_news.title: Cricket: Indian men register five-wicket victory over NZ in first ODI 2 hours ago 168
national_raw_news.content: In Men’s Cricket, India have registered a convincing five-wicket victory over hosts New Zealand in the rain-affected first One-Day International at Auckland, taking a 1-nil lead in the five-match series. Put in to bat first, New Zealand were bowled out by India for 185 runs in 40.2 overs. For the hosts, Tim Seifert top-scored with 38 runs, while Glenn Phillips contributed 30 and Daryl Mitchell made 28. For India, Arshdeep Singh led the bowling attack with four wickets. Gurnoor Brar claimed three wickets, while Anshul Kamboj picked up two. Rain interruptions brought the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern method into play, with a revised target of 143 runs in 32 overs set for India. The visitors made light work of the chase, reaching the target in just 22.4 overs and winning the match by five wickets. The chase was brilliantly anchored by Virat Kohli, who smashed a match-winning 74 off just 51 deliveries. Shubman Gill provided valuable support with 37 runs, while Shreyas Iyer contributed 15. Earlier, India had won the toss and opted to bowl. Kohli also surpassed legendary cricketer Sachin Tendulkar to become the highest run-scorer in ODI chases. His brilliant innings took his total runs while batting to 8,741, moving him past Tendulkar’s 8,720 runs. With this emphatic victory, the visitors will look to carry the winning momentum into the next encounter. The second ODI will be played on Saturday at Wellington. I

national_raw_news.title: RSS annual meeting to conclude today in Indore 3 hours ago 66
national_raw_news.content: The three-day Akhil Bharatiya Karyakari Mandal Meeting of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh concluded in Indore today. RSS chief Dr Mohan Bhagwat, General Secretary Dattatreya Hosabale and around 400 office-bearers and representatives from across the country attended the meeting. The discussions included a review of the Centenary Year programmes, expansion of the organisation, opening of new shakhas and the growing problem of drug addiction among youth. Plans related to education, expansion of RSS activities abroad and taking the Panch Parivartan (five social changes) to the people were also discussed. After the meeting, RSS General Secretary Dattatreya Hosabale addressed the media and spoke on several important issues. On reservation, he said that the system should continue for backward communities as long as social backwardness exists. On the issue of RSS registration, he said that the RSS is a part of society and works according to the laws of the country. Mr Hosabale stressed the need to connect young people with positive activities and keep them away from drug addiction. He said that the younger generation is also falling prey to addiction and RSS volunteers are working to address this issue. He also informed that RSS volunteers had carried out relief work in areas affected by floods and cyclones. In Assam’s Sivasagar and Jorhat districts, more than 1,600 volunteers provided food, water and medicines to around 42,200 families. They also provided support to around 150 families for rebuilding their houses. Help was also provided to farmers, fishermen and other affected families in cyclone-hit areas of Odisha and Andhra Pradesh.

national_raw_news.title: Indo-Pacific Regional Dialogue 2026 begins in New Delhi, focuses on science and technology cooperation
national_raw_news.content: The Indian Navy’s annual apex-level international strategic dialogue, the Indo-Pacific Regional Dialogue 2026 (IPRD-2026), commenced in New Delhi on November 3, with a focus on translating scientific advancement and institutional partnerships into practical regional cooperation. Organised in association with the National Maritime Foundation (NMF), the Navy’s knowledge partner, the three-day conference is being held on the theme ‘Science, Technology and Academic Cooperation in the Indo-Pacific’. The opening day established the central question of the dialogue: how the Indo-Pacific can translate scientific knowledge and technological innovation into enduring institutional cooperation, stronger maritime capabilities and shared regional resilience, according to a press release by the Ministry of Defence. The proceedings began with the inaugural address by Adm Dinesh K Tripathi (Retd), Chairman, NMF, and former Chief of the Naval Staff. This was followed by a special address by VAdm Biswajit Dasgupta (Retd), National Maritime Security Coordinator, Government of India. Academic networks and human capital development The first session focused on ‘Academic Networks, Research, and Human Capital Development’. Moderated by VAdm Sanjay Mahindru (Retd), former Deputy Chief of the Naval Staff, the session featured perspectives from France, Indonesia, Japan and Maldives. It explored the potential for establishing a wider Indian Ocean academic network, including cooperation among universities in Indo-Pacific coastal cities, and examined social-science research networks in the Indian Ocean. The session also discussed closer links among think tanks, universities and governments. A monograph titled ‘Sea Blindness and Maritime Heritage in India’ was released at the conclusion of the session. Maritime domain awareness and protection of critical infrastructure The second professional session, ‘Maritime Situational Awareness and Protection of Critical Maritime Infrastructure’, highlighted contemporary maritime-awareness challenges associated with protecting seaborne trade and critical undersea infrastructure. Moderated by VAdm Tarun Sobti (Retd), former Deputy Chief of the Naval Staff, the session examined the opportunities and challenges associated with the Indo-Pacific Partnership for Maritime Domain Awareness (IPMDA), particularly the practical requirements of information-sharing. It also explored the development of a cooperative Indo-Pacific architecture for underwater domain awareness and included perspectives from the Indian Ocean Commission (IOC) on cooperative approaches to protecting critical maritime infrastructure. Together, the two professional sessions examined how technological systems and scientific partnerships could be made operationally useful by strengthening maritime information-sharing, safeguarding critical infrastructure, improving access to oceanographic knowledge and enabling a more coordinated response to climate-related risks. Special ambassadorial interaction The day’s programme also featured ‘Sahyog Ka Samvaad’, a special ambassadorial interaction with HE Ms Mahishini Colonne, High Commissioner of Sri Lanka; HE Mr Josel F Ignacio, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary, Embassy of the Philippines; and HE Mrs May-Elin Stener, Ambassador of the Kingdom of Norway. The interaction was hosted and moderated by VAdm Pradeep Chauhan (Retd), Director-General, NMF. The first day of IPRD-2026 concluded with enthusiastic audience participation and several actionable policy recommendations on fostering regional cooperation in science and technology and knowledge-sharing through academic collaboration. -PIB Inputs

national_raw_news.content: “Self-reliance is not a retreat from the world; it positions India better for global collaborations”: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर “Self-reliance is not a retreat from the world; it positions India better for global collaborations”: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh ANI | Updated: Nov 04, 2026 00:56 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], November 4 (ANI): Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Tuesday said military preparedness in the 21st century is closely linked to technological and industrial capabilities, emphasising the need for indigenous production of critical equipment and technologies and the capacity to sustain them independently. Addressing the third edition of the Delhi Defence Dialogue at Manohar Parrikar Institute for Defence Studies and Analyses (MP-IDSA) on November 3, he emphasised that ‘Aatmanirbharta’ must be viewed as a quest for technological sovereignty, as self-reliance means ensuring that the nation's critical defence requirements are not held hostage to external dependencies. True self-reliance is achieved by possessing the knowledge to design a defence platform, the technology to manufacture it, intellectual property to improve it and the capability to sustain it throughout its lifecycle, he said. Sharing his insights on the theme of this year's Dialogue, ‘Defence Reforms, Aatmanirbharta, Collaborations and Exports’, the Defence Minister described the four elements as interconnected dimensions of India's objective to become Viksit Bharat by 2047. He stated that reforms must create an enabling institutional environment, Aatmanirbharta must strengthen indigenous technological capabilities, collaborations must accelerate access to advanced technologies and facilitate co-development, and exports must provide the scale, competitiveness and global partnerships required for a sustainable industrial ecosystem. These four elements are mutually reinforcing pillars of India's quest for strategic autonomy, he said. Rajnath Singh underlined that reforms represent the nation's willingness to change, Aatmanirbharta symbolises its determination to create, collaborations reflect its confidence to partner with the world, and exports demonstrate its readiness to compete globally. He emphasised that these four elements must progress together, as self-reliance without reforms, international collaborations and exports would limit India's technological horizons, industrial scale and global competitiveness. The Defence Minister pointed out that recent conflicts across the world have demonstrated a fundamental transformation in the character of warfare, with battlefields extending beyond land, sea and air into space, cyberspace and the digital domain. He stated that the distinction between conventional and unconventional warfare is increasingly blurring, while relatively inexpensive drones and autonomous systems are challenging sophisticated and costly military platforms. The ability to innovate rapidly, manufacture at scale and replenish capabilities has become as important as possessing advanced weapon systems, he added. Highlighting that technological and manufacturing capabilities require an enabling institutional environment, progressive policies and responsive processes, Rajnath Singh outlined the initiatives undertaken over the last decade to strengthen India's domestic defence industrial base. These include the establishment of Defence Industrial Corridors and the corporatisation of the erstwhile Ordnance Factory Board into seven Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs), aimed at enhancing autonomy, efficiency and competitiveness in defence manufacturing.
